chapterTitle: Chapter 1: The Winged Whales resting ground (Ceres)
editorText:
“Thank you Captain”, Tau rose to attention, placing her hands behind her back as brisk strides carried her, her voice carried the room with precision and acumen. “The Storm Rail was initially developed as you know, with rising concerns in the general population of rogue AI tapping into our systems.” Tau knelt down lifting the Storm Rail from it’s precision cut foam holder in it’s case.

 “It has two firing modes in the EMP. The first more conventional brute force approach is a high amplitude EMP, blow their socks off. The second is for more tactful dispersion in high density areas. Directed to first read the operating frequencies of its target and in a preservative respect to its internal battery, And friendly systems in the area impose a resonant frequency to destabilise internal systems of it’s target. And of course if still all else fails you have the kinetic rail, a sequenced firing of charged electron rods along the barrel send a metal slug of your choosing on a warpath to your target, in most cases through it…” Tau paused letting out a slight smirk, “Consider it your own personal cannon, it isn’t far different from the rail turrets on the Balaenoptera used in orbital defence”. “Care to give us a demonstration?” said Tex raising his eyebrows leaning in with his arms crossed pressing forward with his overbearing shoulders. Tau leant down picking up the weapon which weighed not shy of 20Kg, throwing it over John’s shoulder like a sack of potatoes. “You can handle this by yourself without , or with the suit” She gently caressed the Storm rail back and forth till it found a small seat on the shoulder of John’s suit, releasing a small clamping sound. “Unfortunately Big guy, this range isn’t equipped to handle this kind of Fire power, you’ll have to wait till we are in more suitable circumstances, just resort to your training with the first model, but with a little more Kick, I’m sure of all people, you’ll be the first to get the hang of it”, Tau winked at Tex with her last comment, he responded in kind with a flex, splaying out his interwoven fingers in reverse and cracking his neck. “I’m tingling with anticipation!!” chuckled Tex.  “Well as much as we’d love to keep talking about blowing stuff up” Tau dismounted the storm rail from John’s shoulder. He hardly moved upon the motion, as the weight bore down on the suit itself, at least for his sake.  “perhaps.. we should move to putting things back together” Tau was clipping the crate lid back into it’s holder, although she wasn’t looking at the crate, She glared directly across the room at Shai as if to say “Your up!”. As she finished latching the last coupling the crate locked emitting a small low toned beep to signify to it’s user it was secure.
